title: Client Handoff + Triage Landing Pad — Prep & Actions
body:
Purpose / quick context:
- Short: Capture everything I need to run a first 60–90m war-room + clean handoff to SRE/PM/Engineering for critical client incident. This is a personal landing pad — not the official postmortem.

Immediate objectives for first 30 minutes:
- Stabilize communication: confirm channel (slack #client-<org>-incident) and phone bridge if requested.
- Pull latest state: incident JIRA (JIRA-5923), last deploys, error-rate graphs, recent rollouts.
- Decide initial response tier: Is this page-to-oncall? (yes if P1 production outage or data loss).

Key info to gather (fast):
- Who reported and when: inbound from CSM at 08:07 PST, escalated by customer SRE.
- Scope: affected endpoints (/api/v1/generate, /chat-stream), % of traffic impacted ~40% (from dashboards).
- Impact: generation failures and latency >10s for >5% of calls.
- Recent changes: canary deploy 2026-01-17 (model pin + kernel swap) — check commit abc123.

Stakeholders / contacts (order to ping):
- Customer success: Maya Li (primary), Jamal Ortiz (backup) — call first to confirm customer expectations.
- On-call SRE: Omar Patel — priority.
- Serving runtime lead: Priya Menon — technical lead for kernel/model swap rollbacks.
- PM (product): Lina Gomez — for customer comms / timelines.
- Legal/security: if data exposure suspected, loop in security@redwood.

Initial comms templates (copy/paste, personalize):
- To customer (short): "We’ve opened an incident and our on-call is actively investigating. Initial investigations show increased latency affecting ~40% of requests. We’ll provide an update within 30 minutes with next steps. — Rene/Redwood CS"
- Internal Triage post (slack): "INCIDENT: JIRA-5923 — Elevated error/latency on /api/v1/generate. On-call SRE @omar on it. First update in 30m. Key suspects: canary kernel swap (2026-01-17) or KV cache regression. Link to dash: <dashboard-url>"

Triage checklist (first 60 minutes) — check off as done:
- [ ] Confirm incident channel + email thread + phone bridge if requested
- [ ] Snapshot key dashboards (latency, errors, QPS) + time window 30m pre/post spike
- [ ] Collect recent deploys and rollouts (deploy tags, model versions, quantization changes)
- [ ] Ask on-call to run targeted smoke: curl /health, /api/v1/generate with short prompt
- [ ] Check KV cache hit rates and batching latency metrics
- [ ] Validate fallback routes (model-variant, region fallback) are healthy
- [ ] Decide whether to rollback canary or scale dedicated pool

Decision criteria (quick rules):
- Rollback canary if errors spike correlated with canary hosts and rate >5% and customer impact is P1.
- If latency only at tail and local to a region, consider routing around region before rollback.
- If model outputs corrupted (data integrity), escalate to security and consider immediate rollback & disable model.

Action items (assign during call) — populate owners & ETA here:
- Create incident timeline note (owner: Rene) — ETA 20m
- SRE: run kernel/host health checks + attach sample traces (owner: Omar) — ETA 15m
- Runtime lead: validate recent kernel selection & compare perf on canary hosts (owner: Priya) — ETA 30m
- CS: confirm customer tolerance window and preferred comm cadence (owner: Maya) — ETA 10m
- PM: draft customer update if rollback needed (owner: Lina) — ETA 25m

Communication cadence (first 3 hours):
- T+0: Incident opened + customer ack
- T+30: Short internal status update (what we know, next steps)
- T+60: Decision on rollback / mitigation + customer update if impacted
- Every 60m after until stable: status updates, then shift to postmortem planning

Handoff checklist (to SRE/eng for follow-through):
- [ ] Save concrete artifacts: logs, request IDs, sample latencies, core dumps if any
- [ ] Push any agreed rollback through release-engineering checklist (link: confluence://deploy/rollback-steps)
- [ ] Assign postmortem owner once stabilized (preferably non-oncall)

Notes to self / heuristics I've learned:
- Keep comms templated and short; customers want cadence more than details early on.
- Early rollbacks can reduce blast radius but sometimes mask root cause; prefer targeted routing if viable.
- Lean on canary host logs — kernel selection and quantized model ops are frequent culprits for tail latency.

Open questions to resolve in call:
- Is there any scheduled maintenance in infra for the affected region?
- Any customer-side config changes reported recently?
- Are we seeing correlated increase in KV cache misses across models?

After-action quick notes (post-call to fill in):
- What we did (timeline entries) — fill and attach artifacts
- Who was informed and when (customer + execs)
- Short list of follow-ups with owners and deadlines

Scratch area (things I might paste into the incident):
- "Investigations pointing to kernel swap on canary hosts; rolling back canary while preserving traffic to dedicated pool. Temporary mitigation: increase pool size + route 30% away from canary region."
- "Sample request IDs: req_44af, req_44b0, req_44d9 — added to JIRA as attachments."

-- end landing pad --

(If this turns into a long-running incident, migrate notes to shared confluence page and drop this file into customer folder for record.)
